For an example of Joseph Smith rejecting creation ex nihilo, see“Discourse, between circa 26 June and circa 4 August 1839–A, as Reported by Willard Richards,” in Willard Richards Pocket Companion, 64,josephsmithpapers.org. There are also references to ideas expressed in the King Follett discourse in documents that were canonized after Joseph Smith’s lifetime, such as the letter from Liberty Jail that is now included in the Doctrine and Covenants (seeD&C 121:28); teachings at Ramus, Illinois, on April 2, 1843 (seeD&C 130:1, 22); and in the book of Abraham (Abraham 4–5). See also Matthew McBride,“‘Man Was Also in the Beginning with God’: D&C 93,”in Matthew McBride and James Goldberg, eds.,Revelations in Context: The Stories behind the Sections of the Doctrine and Covenants(Salt Lake City: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, 2016), 192–95.
